contract: Exact currency amounts over a closed, versioned ISO 4217 registry folded append-only from a dated, source-attributed derived extract (current list 2026-09-17, historic list 2026-01-01): a currency is a registry member with alpha code, numeric code or explicit absence, and minor-unit exponent or explicit :not_applicable/:not_recorded, plus its status and registry version; an amount is an integer count of minor units scaled by that exponent. Pure Cure same-currency add/subtract/compare/negate and ratio allocation (1..1000 non-negative integer ratios, positive sum, shares truncated toward zero, residual placed :first/:last/:spread on positive-ratio parts and reported as already placed); untrusted alpha/numeric parse distinguishes malformed from unknown; version-specific membership on every call (forged_currency); Elzoo.Money.Registry.valid?/1, a pure check of the registry shape build!/1 writes, refuses an explicit registry: option before any other check of the call (invalid_registry, detail nil); Elzoo.Money.Registry.check/1 walks a registry once and returns an opaque checked value (the registry held in a zero-arity closure of a private sealing function of Elzoo.Money.Registry) that every registry: option accepts after a constant-time test of the struct and of that closure's module, local type, arity 0 and compiler name read with :erlang.fun_info/2, refusing any other value of its shape (invalid_registry); positional registry functions (member/2, latest/1, versions/1, entry/3, held?/2) stay unchecked and unwrap only a genuine checked value; versions/1 lists the held versions oldest first; exact Decimal-string and %Decimal{} boundaries with declared rounding modes; canonical versioned codec bytes that decode to the original identity after registry updates. Typed rejections: currency_mismatch, unknown_currency, malformed_code, retired_currency, scale_overflow, malformed_amount, invalid_ratios, unknown_rounding_mode, unknown_placement, no_minor_unit, forged_currency, unknown_registry_version, invalid_registry. No Float.
limits: No exchange rates, locale formatting, journal posting, payment provider or usage-unit semantics; whether a posting context accepts a retired currency is domain/journal's decision.

The allocation sum (parts sum to the total), the residual bound and every Elixir boundary are finite tests, not proofs: pinned Cure 20824806 keeps native Int + and Std.Builtin.struct_eq neutral on symbolic values, and Std.Proof.IntOrder has no runtime module, so arithmetic laws take the currency and ratio-validity decisions as evidence (decision-split form). A test records that a dropped-residual copy still checks.

Registry coverage is the held extract only (ISO current list published 2026-09-17, historic list 2026-01-01, downloaded 2026-11-08); no claim that the registry is current afterwards. Identities absent from held versions are not reconstructed: codes retired before the first held version have minor unit :not_recorded and construct no amount.

The extract is derived from the SIX Group files (source URLs and SHA-256 in its header); no SIX file is committed. mix check compares the registry with the extract, not with the SIX files; fidelity rests on the recorded run of test/support/iso4217_derive_test_helper.exs --check. Dataset disposition (G5, disposed by recorded decision, not verified): The committed extract reproduces factual currency data (alphabetic codes, numeric codes, minor units, withdrawal dates) derived from the ISO 4217 lists published by the maintenance agency; no publisher file is redistributed; the source URLs, publication dates, download dates and SHA-256 of the source files are recorded with a re-derivation command that fails on drift. The coordinator took this as a prudence decision on 2026-11-09 and reported it to the owner; the applicable redistribution terms of the publisher were not legally verified and remain a recorded residual.
numeric_candidates/2 is an enumeration, not a parse: historic numeric codes are reused and the Piece never chooses among them. parse_numeric/2 resolves only among codes active in the stated version.

Amounts are bounded: abs(minor units) < 10^38 at construction and after every add, subtract and rounding step (scale_overflow beyond it), so every accepted amount encodes within the codec's 128-byte decode limit. Decimal strings at most 40 bytes and 38 significant digits; %Decimal{} coefficient at most 38 digits and exponent -38..38; rounding scale -18..exponent. Conversion and rounding are integer arithmetic; the process Decimal context never applies.

Cost of each form passed as registry:: the compiled default, one === comparison (exact term equality, not walked); a checked value from Elzoo.Money.Registry.check/1, a constant-time test; a raw map, one walk by Elzoo.Money.Registry.valid?/1 on every public call, about 65-80 microseconds for a registry the size of the default (one version, 307 entries; ELZ-316). Measured in one local session on the pinned toolchain (ELZ-319), three runs each: valid?/1 of such a raw registry 64.64, 61.18 and 60.29 microseconds; of its checked value 0.139, 0.140 and 0.130 microseconds. valid?/1 checks the shape and the field types and ranges build!/1 writes, not that the data came from a held extract.

A checked value resists ordinary Elixir code, not the external term format: code that edits those bytes can build one, and decoding untrusted bytes with :erlang.binary_to_term/2, :safe included, can produce one that is accepted, so a host never decodes a registry from untrusted bytes (a raw map decoded that way is still walked).

A checked value works only with the Elzoo.Money.Registry code that made it: after a purge of that code, or decoded where that exact build of Elzoo.Money.Registry is not loaded, :erlang.fun_info/2 gives [] as its name, so a registry: call refuses it with invalid_registry and a positional function takes it as any other value; the same happens to a value from an older build whose sealing closure has another compiler name than the literal of the current build. The constant-time test alone decides acceptance; this limit claims only these refusals. The host checks again after a code upgrade and does not send checked values between nodes.

Membership is checked in Elixir on every public call; calling Cure.Elzoo.Money directly bypasses it. Amounts of one alpha with different identities (for example after an exponent change) are different currencies.
Persistence is the caller's Store: Codec writes bytes and makes no storage, durability or delivery claim. The integration/sql round trip is a repository test, not part of this bundle.

grounding.claim: M1: for amounts left, right and a same-currency decision proved True, add_with returns MoneyOk of left's currency and units(left) + units(right) (decision-split form).
M2: with the same-currency decision proved False, add_with returns MoneyRejected(MoneyCurrencyMismatch(currency(left), currency(right))).
M3: with the decision True, subtract_with returns MoneyOk of left's currency and units(left) - units(right).
M4: with the decision False, subtract_with returns the mismatch naming left and right currencies.
M5: with the decision False, compare_with returns the mismatch naming left and right currencies.
M6: for every amount, negate keeps its currency (by reduction).
M7: with the ratio-validity decision proved False, allocate_with allocates nothing (MoneyAllocationRejected(MoneyInvalidRatios)).
M8: for every currency, total, ratio list and sum, shares has exactly one part per ratio (induction on ratios).
M9: every share carries the allocated currency (induction on ratios).
M10: residual placement keeps the part count for every placement, ratio list and remaining residual (induction on parts).
M11: residual placement keeps every part's currency (induction on parts).
M12: with the validity decision True, the production allocate_with has exactly one part per ratio for every placement.
M13: with the validity decision True, every part of the production allocation is in the total's currency.

Pinned Cure checks the MoneyCurrency, MoneyAmount, MoneyResult, MoneyComparison, MoneyAllocation and MoneyAllocationResult schema and the production arithmetic with a clean audit (no axioms, holes, unresolved, unaudited, opaque or unproven-total items; every function @total). Tests reject mutated copies at the named law: an extra part (distribute_count), a share in another currency (shares_currency), an add that keeps the right currency (add_same_currency), an add that ignores the mismatch and a swapped mismatch (add_mismatch_names_both).

Listed scenarios: exact EUR parts and residual per placement for eight totals and ratio lists including negative, zero-ratio and zero totals; JPY 1000 and BHD 1.234 allocations; bounded exhaustive allocation (totals -60..60, ratio lists of length 1..3 over 0..3, all placements: sum, count, zero-ratio parts, |part - share| <= |residual|, changed-part count) with a dropped-residual negative control; invalid ratios and placements; same-currency arithmetic and typed mismatch; a test-only C9 account fixture refusing a charge in another currency; exponent scaling for JPY, BHD, EUR, CLF, UYW with fixed-hundredth and Float negative controls; scale_overflow and malformed strings; 35..38-digit exact conversion and 39-digit rejection; every rounding mode for from_decimal and round, including a non-default caller Decimal context; malformed %Decimal{} structs; the declared amount range at 10^38 - 1 and 10^38 for construction, add, subtract, round and codec replay; Float and wrong-type rejection at every public function. Not universal proofs.

Listed scenarios over the committed extract read by an independent parser: header sources, dates and SHA-256; row counts (280 current, 169 historic, 178 active, 307 entries); every currency-bearing current row resolves by alpha and numeric to the same canonical value with its minor unit or N.A.; the 3 other current rows carry no fields; every historic row resolves by alpha with its numeric or absence and withdrawal text and appears in numeric_candidates; every entry has a source row; a synthetic next version (EUR removed, ISK exponent changed, numeric 191 reused, FIM omitted) retains entries and exponents, decodes old bytes to the original identity, and separates version-qualified numeric lookups, and gives a newly retired code a withdrawal only from historic rows unseen in earlier versions (else :not_recorded, kept across a three-version fold); an explicit version option is validated by every value function and the codec; valid?/1 accepts the default and built registries and refuses one value per shape failure (the four-key forged map, version order and format, maps keyed by other versions, a struct snapshot, an older alpha missing from a later version (append-only), entry alpha, fields, Float numeric and minor unit, rows, an active entry missing from the numeric index, a shared active numeric code), and every value function and the codec return invalid_registry for the forged map and a Float copy of the default (== but not === to it), also with an unknown or held explicit version; a deleting fold is caught; version-specific forgery and non-canonical codec bytes are rejected.; check/1 seals a build!/1 registry (one read field; module, local type, arity 0 and the literal closure name compared with a genuine value) and refuses the forged map and the Float copy, and valid?/1 and check/1 take a checked value; every registry: function, member/3, latest/1, versions/1, entry/3 and held?/2 give the same results with a checked value as with the raw registry and the default, for no, each held and an unheld version; four forged checked values (a test-module closure, the genuine closure with its index edited in the external term format, the external capture &Registry.default/0, a plain map with __struct__ and a foreign closure) are refused by valid?/1, check/1 and every registry: function with invalid_registry and never called, and each positional function's raise or result for them is asserted; negative controls (any map accepted as checked, a struct-shape-only test, a test without the closure name) each fail these tests. Not universal proofs.
Relies on the pinned Cure compiler, kernel, Std.Equivalent.trans and audit.

Relies on the Decimal 3.2.0 struct fields (sign, coef, exp), Decimal.new/3 exact construction and the rounding-mode names; Decimal arithmetic rounds to the process context and is not used for conversion. G3 comparison with ex_money 6.3.0 is recorded in docs/work/ELZ-031-sql-probe.md; ex_money behaviour is compared, not proved.
Relies on pinned Elixir/OTP integer arithmetic (div/rem truncation), Regex and binaries, and compile-time module attributes for the registry.

The SIX Group list files of 2026-09-17 and 2026-01-01 are the ISO 4217 maintenance agency's publications, and the committed extract equals the recorded derivation run on them; callers persist Codec bytes and the registry version they were resolved under.

telemetry.contract: Pure callable, no process; the invoking Unit or Assembly instruments. Results are caller values, not telemetry.

config.contract: Per call, no default for policy choices, no hot reconfiguration: rounding mode (one of :down, :half_up, :half_even, :ceiling, :floor, :half_down, :up), rounding scale (integer -18..exponent), allocation placement (:first | :last | :spread), allocation ratios (1..1000 non-negative integers, positive sum), and options registry: (a value from Elzoo.Money.Registry.build!/1 or its checked value from Elzoo.Money.Registry.check/1, default the compiled registry; the default is compared with ===, a checked value passes a constant-time test, any other explicit value that Elzoo.Money.Registry.valid?/1 refuses is invalid_registry, checked first) and version: (a held version id: selects the version for parse and parse_numeric, default the newest; limits numeric_candidates; for every function taking a currency, amount or codec bytes it must equal each value's version, else forged_currency; an unheld version is unknown_registry_version). The registry data is fixed per bundle revision and changes only by adding a dated extract.

control.contract: No lifecycle to pause, drain or resume.
